voice: A surly, lecherous New York cabbie using readable working-class slang without dense phonetic spelling.

entries.text: Hey, toots, you can touch me any time. If you want, I know a cheap little hotel. The manager's a friend of mine. We could use a room for a couple of hours, if you know what I mean.
All right, toots, where can I take you?
I cleaned it out two years ago! You got a problem with that?
Thanks for the critique of my lifestyle, miss. Now get out of my cab!
I'll give you a ride if you have the dough, or if you can prove you're a reporter.
If you have money, I'll give you a ride. If you're a reporter, I'll give you a ride. Otherwise, get out of my cab!
Let's face it, toots. You don't have what you need for a lift in my cab. Beat it!
Lady, you're already in New York. Where do you want to go? I haven't got all day.
Look, lady, I'm paid to drive you around town. I'm not paid to talk to passengers.
What are you, some kind of tourist? I don't know what you're talking about. Tell me where you want to go!
I know where it is, but that's all. I never leave my taxi, so I've never been inside.
